verdict.rationale: Penpot's docs say components can be reused across files, and that copies stay linked so changes to the Main component flow to them. That covers the core of cross-file component reuse with source-driven updates. The evidence never describes publishing a shared library, sharing styles across projects, or a controlled review/accept flow for updates. Community remarks that its design-system features trail Figma are general and do not contradict the documented behavior. Missing for 10: explicit shared-library publish/connect workflow, cross-project scope, shared styles (colors/typography) via libraries, controlled update review/accept mechanism, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a designer, shared libraries publish components and styles across files and projects, with controlled updates when the source changes

citations.quote: A component is a layer or group of layers that can be reused multiple times across files.
All component copies used in a file are linked in a way that updates made to the Main component can reflect in their component copies.
